title: MIMIC-CXR, a de-identified publicly available database of chest radiographs with free-text reports
why_seed: Large public chest radiograph dataset with free-text reports; useful as a dataset anchor when checking whether VLM work is single-timepoint or longitudinal.
known_claims: Provides chest radiographs paired with radiology reports.
Often used as a foundation dataset for medical vision-language modeling.
known_limitations: The dataset itself is not a lesion-level temporal change benchmark by default.
Lesion masks and explicit paired-change labels require additional construction.

title: CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
why_seed: A common chest X-ray classification benchmark; useful as a counterpoint because it emphasizes image-level labels rather than lesion-level temporal change reasoning.
known_claims: Provides large-scale chest radiograph labels with uncertainty handling.
known_limitations: Not designed as a paired longitudinal lesion-change benchmark.
Does not directly evaluate lesion localization consistency.

title: MedCLIP: Contrastive Learning from Unpaired Medical Images and Text
why_seed: Representative medical vision-language pretraining work; useful for checking whether generic image-text alignment covers temporal lesion comparison.
known_claims: Uses unpaired medical images and text for contrastive learning.
known_limitations: Temporal paired-study reasoning is not the central evaluation target.
Lesion-level change evidence is not the default supervision signal.

title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
why_seed: Representative biomedical VLM assistant; useful for checking whether instruction-tuned medical VLMs evaluate paired temporal lesion change rather than general biomedical QA/chat.
known_claims: Adapts large vision-language assistants to biomedical image-text instruction following.
known_limitations: The main setting is not specifically lesion-localized temporal comparison.
Benchmarking temporal paired-study change reasoning requires additional evaluation design.
